title: Private Endpoints & Private DNS in Azure

scenes.line1: Why does your app still hit public IPs?
scenes.line2: Is your DNS set up right?
scenes.say: Ever created a private endpoint, but your app still connects to a public address? Is your DNS actually routing traffic where you want?

scenes.label: Endpoint
scenes.sub: Private endpoint gives a service a private IP in your VNet.
scenes.say: A private endpoint assigns a private IP to a service right inside your virtual network. That keeps traffic internal and secure.
Here's how DNS should work: your app asks for the service name, gets a special privatelink alias, and that resolves to the private IP.
Service endpoints keep the public IP and stay on Azure's backbone. Private endpoints give you a private IP, but you need private DNS for name resolution.

scenes.question: App still hits public IP after endpoint?
scenes.right: You must link the private DNS zone to your VNet, or set up DNS forwarding from on-prem to Azure DNS.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: creating a private endpoint isn't enough. If DNS isn't set up, your app still connects to the public IP.
